sent Harthama and Tahir, the generals of the armies, to Baghdad.
And the people of Baghdad were split into two factions,
and panic fell upon the whole city.
And they would even enter the palaces of the kings and plunder gold and garments;
and they also pillaged one another and committed violence.
And because there are no stones in Baghdad,
they began to break up the columns of the churches and shoot them with catapults.
And when Amin saw these things,
he sent to Harthama asking him to swear an oath to him concerning his life and his belongings;
and he swore to him.
Tahir, however, when he heard, became enraged;
and he stationed guards, and they caught Amin at night while he was fleeing in a boat.
He, however, threw himself into the river, swam, and escaped,
and hid in the house of a poor man.
And when he was found there, he was killed,
and his head was fixed upon a spear,
and carried around Baghdad on a Sunday,
the fifth of Muharram,
the year one hundred and ninety-eight of the Hagarenes (813 of our Lord).
After Amin, Ma'mun his brother, for twenty and a half years.
This one sent and had Harthama, the general,
who had sworn to Amin,
brought to him in Khurasan,
and he put him to death.
And his companions were zealous,
and went into the bathhouse,
and killed the one who had killed him.
And Ma'mun commanded and crucified {impaled} them.
Then Nasr the rebel gathered the Qaysites,
and went against the Tanukhites who were encamped by the river Quwayq at Aleppo.
And they waged war with them for ten days.
And the Tanukhites were weakened,
and by night the men and women decamped to Qinnasrin.
And the Qaysites and the people of Aleppo entered,
and plundered their great dwellings which were full of wealth and merchandise.
And just as a short while earlier they had been stripped of their faith,
so now also they departed from their wealth barefoot and naked.
And after these things, Tahir, the general of Ma'mun, arrived with four thousand Persians at Callinicus,
and pursued the rebels.
And he, too, even more than the rebels, increased the tributes,
and did evil to the people of Sarug and Edessa,
until his companions gathered against him to kill him,
because he withheld their rations from them.
And when he perceived it,
he threw himself down from the wall and fled to Callinicus.
And in the morning, when his companions realized it,
they feared lest Nasr should overtake them,
